title: Inherited Hardware Wallet: Unknown PIN, Reset Advice, and a Dead Device
plain:
If the device asks for a PIN you don't have, do not reset it. Stop guessing and find the backup words first: repeated wrong entries can lock the device, and resetting without the seed phrase backup destroys access to the bitcoin forever. Look for a card or paper word list kept with the device or with important documents.

If someone says hardware wallets should be reset before recovering so no one else's data remains, don't — never reset a device you did not set up yourself. A reset erases its keys; only the seed phrase backup can restore them. Check for the seed phrase backup before touching the device; with it you can always recover, and without it a reset is final.

If the screen is cracked and the device won't turn on, don't panic: no — the bitcoin is on the blockchain, not in the device. The seed phrase can restore the wallet on a new device, even from a different brand. Do not try to repair or open it yourself yet. Keep the device safe and unchanged while you find the backup.

In every case the order is the same: find and verify the backup words first, then handle hardware. Never type the backup words into any website, app, or message, and never share them with anyone who contacts you.
technical:
A hardware wallet is a signing device, not a store of funds: balances live on the blockchain, and the device's secure element only holds the private keys. PIN lockouts are anti-brute-force protection, not deletion, but any reset — deliberate or triggered on some models by repeated failed attempts — clears the keys from the secure element; only the BIP-39 seed phrase backup can regenerate them. An heir should treat the backup's existence as unverified until it is located and checked.

A dead or damaged device does not affect the funds: the seed phrase can reconstruct the wallet on any BIP-39-compatible device, including another brand. Do not attempt repair or teardown before the backup situation is resolved; tampering can complicate later secure-element inspection if recovery ever depends on it.
